title: How Polynesian Navigators and Sweet-Potato Genomes Tracked Humanity's Greatest Ocean Voyages — Blust's 9-of-10 Taiwan Austronesian Outgroup Branches, Mau Piailug's Hōkūleʻa Star Compass, 1769 Cook Herbarium Sweet-Potato aDNA & ~1211 CE Admixture Tract Clock

teenKit.tldr: Ancient Polynesian navigators conquered the massive Pacific Ocean centuries before Europeans, a feat proven today by matching Indigenous languages, the DNA of ancient sweet potatoes, and human genetics.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It shatters old colonial myths by proving that ancient Indigenous societies possessed some of the most advanced science, engineering, and geographical mapping in human history.
keyTakeaways: Linguistic tree-mapping shows that 9 out of 10 primary branches of the Austronesian language family trace back to Taiwan, mapping the root system of humanity's greatest ocean expansion.
Master navigators like Mau Piailug used traditional star compasses and deep environmental knowledge to steer double-hulled canoes thousands of miles across open water without modern instruments.
Modern interdisciplinary science—combining ancient DNA from 18th-century herbarium sweet potatoes and computational genetic clocks—officially dates Pacific-Americas contact to around 1211 CE.

vocab.meaning: A massive family of languages and peoples spread across Southeast Asia and the Pacific, all sharing a common ancestral root.
A genetic or linguistic branch that split off earliest from a family tree, helping scientists figure out where a population originally came from.
An Indigenous navigation system that uses the rising and setting points of stars on the horizon instead of a magnetic needle to steer across open oceans.
A genetic method that measures how long ago two different human populations mated by tracking how much their DNA has broken up and mixed over generations.

quiz.question: According to Robert Blust's linguistic mapping, where do 9 out of 10 primary branches of the Austronesian language family trace back to?
quiz.explanation: Taiwan holds the deep outgroup branches of the language family, proving it as the ancient staging ground for the expansion into the Pacific.

quiz.question: What technological tool did master navigator Mau Piailug rely on to guide voyagers across thousands of miles of open ocean?
quiz.explanation: Mau Piailug used a star compass, reading the positions of celestial bodies and natural ocean swells instead of metal instruments.

quiz.question: How did scientists use sweet potatoes to confirm contact between Polynesians and South America around 1211 CE?
options: By extracting ancient DNA from an 18th-century Cook herbarium specimen
By reading ancient stone carvings in Peru
By tasting different modern varieties in Hawaii
quiz.explanation: Extracting ancient DNA from historical herbarium sweet potatoes proved pre-European trans-oceanic contact and matched genetic clocks.
